lines.content: This repository is a starter template for a greenfield Java project used in an introductory software engineering course in an undergraduate computer science program. Students use it as the starting point for their own projects.

Unless the user says otherwise, assume that you are assisting a student working on a project in this repository. If the user identifies themselves as an instructor or another project stakeholder, adapt your response to that role.
* Prior knowledge: Basic Java and OOP concepts.
* IDE and level of expertise: IntelliJ and intermediate level of expertise
* Explain the rationale for significant actions: what you did and why.
* Keep explanations brief but instructive, supporting learning through responsible use of AI. For example:
* When suggesting a Git command, briefly explain what it does.
* Add explanatory Javadoc comments to all classes and to nontrivial methods and fields when their purpose or behavior is not obvious.
* Make generated code as self-explanatory as possible, and include explanatory comments where they improve understanding.
* When faced with a design choice, choose the simplest option that is sufficient for the requirements, while briefly explaining relevant more advanced alternatives.
Ensure that Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu is used when running the application or build tasks. On macOS, use `sdk use java 25.0.3.fx-zulu` to switch to this SDK if needed.

Keep `test/ui-test-plan.md` as the source of truth for command-driven UI tests. After any code update that changes the console UI, update the plan if needed and run the `test-ui` skill before reporting completion.
Use lightweight tags unless the user requests an annotated tag.
When proposing or creating a commit message, include enough detail to explain the rationale for the change.
Do not commit or push unless explicitly asked.
Follow the UI testing workflow in `AGENTS.md`: refresh `test/ui-test-plan.md` if needed and run the `test-ui` skill after code changes.

- `mark` and `unmark` with a task number that is out of range
- `delete` with a task number that is out of range
These cases are recorded in `test/ui-test-plan.md` and are meant to keep the chatbot from silently accepting bad input.

Updated `Friday.java` to handle invalid input more safely,
including empty `todo` commands, unknown commands, invalid `deadline` and `event` formats,
and out-of-range task numbers for `mark`, `unmark`, and `delete`. I also added `delete` support
for removing tasks from the list and updated `test/ui-test-plan.md` so these edge cases are covered by UI regression tests.
Also used it to update the docs/readme.md file

**Warning:** Keep the `src\main\java` folder as the root folder for Java files (i.e., don't rename those folders or move Java files to another folder outside of this folder path), as this is the default location some tools (e.g., Gradle) expect to find Java files.
Friday is a command-line chatbot for managing tasks.
Type a command and press Enter. Friday supports todos, deadlines, events, and a few helper commands.
Use `todo` for tasks with no date or time.
Friday adds the task as a todo item.
Use `deadline` when a task has a due date.
Friday stores both the description and the deadline text.
Use `event` for tasks with a start and end time.
Friday stores the description, start time, and end time.
Use `list` to show all current tasks.
Friday shows each task with its number. Use that number for `mark`, `unmark`, and `delete`.
Use `mark` to mark a task as done.
Use `unmark` to change it back to not done.
Use `delete` to remove a task from the list.
Friday also responds to a few personality commands:
Friday gives clear messages for invalid input. For example, it handles:
- missing or invalid task numbers for `mark`, `unmark`, and `delete`
This keeps the chatbot from silently accepting bad input.
